newsitem.title: USA: Rubin faces queries over political meet with banks.
newsitem.headline: Rubin faces queries over political meet with banks.

text.p: Senate Majority leader Trent Lott on Sunday raised questions about Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's participation in a controversial White House meeting last year with bankers and Democratic Party fundraisers.
"I think it's very questionable," the Mississippi Republican told ABC television's "This Week" news program.
Rubin, President Clinton and Comptroller of the Currency Eurgene Ludwig attended the May 1996 meeting over coffee with more than a dozen leading bankers and Democratic fundraisers.
Some of the bankers pumped more than $300,000 into Clinton's campaign after the meeting.
Ludwig, who is responsible for regulating many of the country's biggest banks, has said since that he should not have attended the meeting -- and Clinton has agreed.
Interviewed on the same news program, Rubin defended his participation in the meeting, saying he was not a regulator.
"I prepared for a policy meeting, I attended a meeting that I viewed as a policy discussion, and that's exactly what we engaged in," the Treasury chief said.

Lott though was not convinced. "You've got the Comptroller and the Secretary of the Treasury in a meeting with those that are regulated ... and fundraisers at the White House," he said. "That is not good. It may be illegal."
